reviews.reading_evidence: Read all five source/target stanzas: sleeping in Mother’s lap without sleep, her silence and absent lullaby, laughing flowers and vanished butterflies, blood and culpability, children as her regrets/sorrows, Gaza/Ukraine/Murshidabad cries explaining silence, and the final shameless sleep with open eyes while silence may last forever. Preserved the collective indictment and paradox rather than treating sleep as a factual inconsistency.
reviews.reason: In this indictment, बेधड़क describes untroubled indifference. Replace fearlessly with without a care so the continued sleep is not mistaken for courage.
reviews.tradeoff: The target loses the positive implication of fearlessness and retains the collective failure to respond; no identity for Mother or historical fact is supplied.

reviews.reason: Use a natural English predicate for बयान करता है; speak the reason is an introduced calque. Keep the three place-linked cries as the explaining subject.
reviews.tradeoff: Revealing remains the work of the cries, not an added narrator explanation; stanza and line counts unchanged.

reviews.reading_evidence: Read both complete twenty-line stanzas: refusal of chiming bangles then tinkling anklets, their repeated binding/bonds feeling, request for roses then tuberoses, fragrance filling the inner self, and repeated consciousness of freedom. Retain the contrast and deliberately near-identical recurrence; no marriage or biographical circumstance is inferred.
reviews.reason: Retain the direct request/refusal and repeated scent/freedom construction; no defensible meaning correction needed.
reviews.tradeoff: Keep the source’s repeated experience/feeling wording and short lines rather than reducing the refrain to a slogan.

reviews.reading_evidence: Read five four-line stanzas and the Jamshedpur tail: complaint to an unmoved traveller, searching eyes and tired tears, feet rushing at every sound, unspoken longing and invitation to plumb the heart, letters addressed with the heart, dyer/colour request, red gulmohar and yellow amaltas, green earth and seven-coloured veil. Checked the source’s feminine expressions without inventing a relationship history.
reviews.reason: Replace two unadapted Hindi lexical carryovers with ordinary Odia pain and sound while preserving the body’s anxious responses.
open_questions: मिली नहीं remains provisionally not meeting the traveller; the unexpressed object/attachment is unresolved.
Rangrez is retained as dyer/colourer without asserting a religious figure or hidden identity.
reviews.tradeoff: ବେଦନା is less sharply onomatopoeic than टीस; the aching eyes/tears context carries the hurt. ଶବ୍ଦ retains an unspecified audible cue without inventing footsteps.

prior_uncertainties.note: ମିଳିନଥିବା/never met is a provisional reading of मिली नहीं; no backstory added. Rangrez/dyer and flower colours preserved. Closing address retained.

reviews.reading_evidence: Read five four-line stanzas and the Jamshedpur tail: complaint to an unmoved traveller, searching eyes and tired tears, feet rushing at every sound, unspoken longing and invitation to plumb the heart, letters addressed with the heart, dyer/colour request, red gulmohar and yellow amaltas, green earth and seven-coloured veil. reviews.reason: In the repeated accusation of forgetting the speaker and ignoring pain, निर्मोही addresses emotional unresponsiveness. Unattached can imply relationship status or admirable renunciation, weakening the complaint; revise title and opening together.
open_questions: मिली नहीं remains provisionally not meeting the traveller; the unexpressed object/attachment is unresolved.
Rangrez is retained as dyer/colourer without asserting a religious figure or hidden identity.
निर्मोही can also carry detachment/renunciation; unfeeling is the contextual complaint reading, not author-confirmed.
reviews.tradeoff: Unfeeling sharpens the ordinary English complaint while avoiding the harsher heartless; preserve dyer and cultural flowers without explanation.

reviews.reading_evidence: Read the two cloud stanzas and closing couplet: repeated Time is a dense cloud, many rains and earth’s sure-footed reassurance/gusto, a gust dissolving the cloud and unlived breaths, wisps conveying sky’s illusion/gloom, then countless versus cipher holding many lives/deaths. Compared negation, capability, sound clusters and the earth/sky opposition in the full current target.
reviews.reason: Render gust as a sudden movement of wind; the existing ଝାଙ୍କ wording does not naturally name that action. Preserve mere touch and immediate vanishing.
open_questions: Unlived breaths remains intentionally strange; the exact reach of unlived/ଅଜିଆଁ awaits fluent review, not normalized to unbreathed or dead.
reviews.tradeoff: ଦଲକା keeps the wind movement concrete without adding a storm. The source’s cipher is read as zero in the countless contrast, not decoded as a secret message.

reviews.reason: Retain the complete target’s cloud repetition, immediate gust-touch, unlived breaths, gnawing gloom and countless/zero contrast; no independent correction needed.
reviews.tradeoff: Keep श्वास and the unusual unlived adjective as poetic language; do not replace the source’s uncertainty with a conventional life/death lesson.

reviews.reason: Retain the concise rhetorical contrast and final wasteland accusation; no new independent correction justified.
